QF.id: AIFM CIII Legal Documents and Negotiations_2

question.text: Ms. Priya Shah, CIO of Aravalli Long-Short Fund, is deciding the legal form for a new Cat III scheme. The primary reason most Indian AIFs (including Cat III) are set up as TRUSTS rather than companies is:

answer.text: A trust enjoys pass-through taxation under Section 115UB which is not available to companies.
A trust allows ring-fencing of the Investment Manager's liability since the Manager is only a counterparty service provider and not a director or designated partner.
A trust is exempt from the 2x leverage cap that applies to companies.
A trust structure automatically qualifies for Section 10(4D) at IFSC without any extra filings.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Chapter 9.3 explicitly states that a trust structure permits ring-fencing of the Manager's liability (including fiduciary/breach-of-fund-documents liability) because the Manager is only a counterparty service provider, unlike being on the Board of a company AIF or a designated partner in an LLP. This is why the majority of Indian AIFs are trusts. **The Trap:** Option A is a Cat I/II myth — Cat III is taxed at FUND LEVEL at MMR (AOP), Section 115UB does NOT apply to Cat III. Option C fabricates a leverage carve-out; 2x is form-neutral. Option D invents automatic IFSC exemption. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-D (Cat I/II Manager) focused on pass-through via 115UB. XIX-E Cat III has fund-level MMR, so the taxation argument is reversed. XIX-C (All-Cat) expects candidates to flag this difference. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** For a Cat III hedge fund, the trust form also simplifies side-pocket accounting and daily-NAV series-of-units creation (not possible cleanly under Companies Act share-capital rules). Keep the indenture silent on daily operations — delegate them to the IMA.
